title: an approval swaps the rulesets' working copy whole, and the reader refuses a read that is not whole
note: basis 'shown' means shown by tests/unit/test_ruleset_swap_int_r3a.py at master 6c73db64 (the file copied in) and at the card's head, in a session container; 'read' means read in the code, not run.

findings.claim: RulesetRepo.materialize removed a ruleset's working copy, then renamed the new one in, and load_approved returned whatever it had read: with two reader processes and 200 approvals, 20 reads found no file, 15 loads were partial rulesets and 16 found no manifest; the copy is now exchanged in one rename and a read that differs from the approval tag's tree is refused as RulesetReadIncomplete (0 of each in three runs)

the swap needs Linux renameat2 with RENAME_EXCHANGE; where the kernel or the file system has none the approval fails after its tag and main commit are written and the old copy stays whole; there is no fallback

fault type 2 outside the approval path, not fixed: materialize of a ruleset gone from its ref still removes the working copy in place (shutil.rmtree), and seed_working_copy copies the shipped rulesets into the folder in place (copytree)

list_rulesets globs */manifest.yaml with pathlib, which matches hidden names: while a materialisation runs, .<ruleset>.tmp is listed as a ruleset id (load_approved refuses it: no approval tag); not fixed

omop.vocab_load.mark_rulesets reads each working copy with Ruleset.load, unchecked against the approval tag, to mark rulesets for recompilation; it uses only the manifest, which the swap now keeps whole, but a read that meets a swap can end in a FileNotFoundError, caught as OSError, and that ruleset is not marked on that load; not fixed
